findings.observed: Requires dynamic-mcp-actions-support feature and Windows developer mode. MCP app data toggles tool integration.
findings.conclusion: MCP tools can extend the orchestrator; they do not replace its inference provider.

assessment.consumer_direct_alzette_model: No supported integration found; no working custom-backend qualification.
assessment.experimental_local_service_emulation: A possible research direction suggested by the local service selector, not a demonstrated integration. Requires Copilot-specific service protocol, session/bootstrap and tool lifecycle emulation, plus a reachable endpoint selection mechanism. A gateway-only OpenAI/Anthropic adapter is insufficient.
assessment.m365_custom_engine_agent: Officially supports own AI models and orchestration; an Alzette-backed agent is architecturally feasible. Separate enterprise app/hosted agent project, not consumer backend replacement; not live-tested without a Microsoft 365 tenant/app registration.
assessment.windows_agent_launchers: Official system discovery/invocation for own agent; does not replace consumer Copilot inference.
assessment.reverse_direction_projects: Windows-Copilot-API consumes Microsoft Copilot and serves an OpenAI-compatible facade to other clients. It does not let the Copilot app consume Alzette.

recommended_scope: Ship the native Claude/ChatGPT integration already qualified. If Microsoft 365 customers need Alzette inside Copilot, build a custom engine agent; do not advertise consumer Copilot BYOK support.
